<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We assume that the FedIT and each local model exhibit LMC within the LMC basin, i.e., the entire linear interpolation path between them remains inside the basin.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_assumption">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption 3.2</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{\delta}</annotation></semantics></math> be the LMC basin in Definition <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Definition 3.1. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>. For each client <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, we assume that
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\,\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}+\lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{Local}}\,\bm{\theta}^{(i)}_{\mathrm{Local}}\;\in\;\mathcal{U}_{\delta},\quad\forall\,\lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{Local}}\geq 0,\ \lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}+\lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{Local}}=1." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Local</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">∀</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\,\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}+\lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{Local}}\,\bm{\theta}^{(i)}_{\mathrm{Local}}\;\in\;\mathcal{U}_{\delta},\quad\forall\,\lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{Local}}\geq 0,\ \lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}+\lambda^{(i)}_{\mathrm{Local}}=1.</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Throughout our analysis, we focus on the behavior of the loss landscape within the LMC basin and make the following standard assumptions on optimization.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_assumption">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption 3.3</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The task loss function <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}</annotation></semantics></math> is locally Lipschitz smooth within the LMC basin <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{\delta}</annotation></semantics></math>.
There exist constants <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that</p>
<table id="S3.EGx7" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{y})\leq\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x})+\nabla\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x})^{\top}(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x})+\frac{L}{2}\|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{y})\leq\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x})+\nabla\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x})^{\top}(\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x})+\frac{L}{2}\|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|^{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.E7"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\forall\,\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\in\mathcal{U}_{\delta}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">∀</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐲</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\forall\,\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\in\mathcal{U}_{\delta}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Equivalently, the Hessian of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded within the LMC basin, i.e., <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x})\preceq L\,\mathbf{I},\,\forall\,\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{U}_{\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mo>∇</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⪯</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐈</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">∀</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x})\preceq L\,\mathbf{I},\,\forall\,\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{U}_{\delta}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_assumption">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption 3.4</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nesterov and Polyak, 2006</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Carmon et al., 2018</a>)</cite>
The Hessian of the task loss within the LMC basin is <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{H}</annotation></semantics></math>-Lipschitz continuous if <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{y})-\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x})\|\leq L_{H}\|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|,\forall\,\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\in\mathcal{U}_{\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">∀</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{y})-\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x})\|\leq L_{H}\|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|,\forall\,\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\in\mathcal{U}_{\delta}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{H}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{H}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> is a constant.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In the following, we show that the model obtained by merging the FedIT model and the local model yields a personalized performance gain.
For clarity, we omit the client index.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We use the Laplace approximation to approximate the task vectors of FedIT (i.e., <math id="S3.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math>) and local fine-tuning (i.e., <math id="S3.SS3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math>) as Gaussian distributions:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx8" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E8"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\sim\mathcal{N}(\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sim\mathcal{N}(\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.E9"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\sim\mathcal{N}(\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}},\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sim\mathcal{N}(\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}},\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p5.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the MAP parameter estimates of the corresponding task vectors, and
<math id="S3.SS3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}=\mathbf{F}_{\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}}^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐅</mi><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}=\mathbf{F}_{\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}}^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}=\mathbf{F}_{\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}}^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐅</mi><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}=\mathbf{F}_{\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}}^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> are given by the inverses of their Fisher information matrices.
The full derivation is provided in Appendix <a href="#A1.SS1" title="A.1 Derivation of Gaussian Distribution Approximation ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Results ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p">We further assume a joint Gaussian distribution of FedIT and local task vectors, which introduces an explicit cross-covariance term.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_assumption">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption 3.5</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>
We assume that <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}})</annotation></semantics></math> follow a joint Gaussian distribution:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx9" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E10"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\\
\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}}\end{bmatrix}\sim\mathcal{N}\bigg(\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\\
\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}&amp;\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\\
\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}^{\top}&amp;\bm{\Sigma}_{\text{Local}}\end{bmatrix}\bigg)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msubsup><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mtext>Local</mtext></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\\
\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}}\end{bmatrix}\sim\mathcal{N}\bigg(\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\\
\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}&amp;\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\\
\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}^{\top}&amp;\bm{\Sigma}_{\text{Local}}\end{bmatrix}\bigg),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the cross-covariance matrix between the two task vectors.
We assume that FedIT task and local task are correlated, therefore, the cross-covariance matrix satisfies <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\succeq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪰</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\succeq 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Furthermore, we assume that <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪯</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪯</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The conditions <math id="S3.SS3.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪯</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪯</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math> indicate that the cross-covariance is not larger than the marginal variances, i.e., the shared uncertainty does not dominate each model’s own uncertainty.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p8.1" class="ltx_p">With the joint Gaussian model in Assumption <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem5" title="Assumption 3.5. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a>, we can derive the Gaussian distribution of the merged task vector:</p>

<p id="S3.SS3.p8.2" class="ltx_p">where</p>
<table id="S3.EGx11" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<div id="S3.SS3.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p9.1" class="ltx_p">We now present an expected excess loss bound for FedIT, Local, and their merged model.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.6</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Under Definition <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Definition 3.1. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>, Assumption <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Assumption 3.2. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>, <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Assumption 3.3. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>, <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem4" title="Assumption 3.4. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a>, and <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem5" title="Assumption 3.5. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a>, for <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{\mathrm{FedIT},\mathrm{Local},\mathrm{Merge}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>FedIT</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Local</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Merge</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{\mathrm{FedIT},\mathrm{Local},\mathrm{Merge}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, it holds that</span></p>
<table id="S3.EGx12" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex5"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\theta}_{i})-\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})\right]\leq\bigg(\frac{L}{2}+\frac{L_{H}}{6}\delta\bigg)\delta^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\theta}_{i})-\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})\right]\leq\bigg(\frac{L}{2}+\frac{L_{H}}{6}\delta\bigg)\delta^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.E14"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad+\bigg(\frac{L}{2}+\frac{L_{H}}{6}\delta\bigg)\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{i})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad+\bigg(\frac{L}{2}+\frac{L_{H}}{6}\delta\bigg)\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{i}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Proof sketch of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem6" title="Theorem 3.6. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.6</span></a>.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To bound the expected excess loss, we expand <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}</annotation></semantics></math> around the optimum <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\phi}=\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}}-\mathbf{W}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\phi}=\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}}-\mathbf{W}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}=\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}=\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>.
By Lemma 2.2 in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Carmon et al., 2018</a>)</cite>, we have</p>
<table id="S3.EGx13" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E15"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}\!+\!\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}})\!\leq\!\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})\!\!+\!\tfrac{1}{2}\bm{\phi}^{\top}\mathbf{H}\bm{\phi}\!+\!\tfrac{L_{H}}{6}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.052em">+</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mpadded style="width:0.271em;" width="0.271em"><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mpadded></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.052em">+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.052em" rspace="0.052em">+</mo><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}\!+\!\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}})\!\leq\!\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})\!\!+\!\tfrac{1}{2}\bm{\phi}^{\top}\mathbf{H}\bm{\phi}\!+\!\tfrac{L_{H}}{6}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">By
<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\bm{\phi}^{\top}\mathbf{H}\bm{\phi}]\!=\!(\mathbb{E}\bm{\phi})^{\top}\mathbf{H}(\mathbb{E}\bm{\phi})+\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{H}\,\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{\phi}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Cov</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\bm{\phi}^{\top}\mathbf{H}\bm{\phi}]\!=\!(\mathbb{E}\bm{\phi})^{\top}\mathbf{H}(\mathbb{E}\bm{\phi})+\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{H}\,\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{\phi}))</annotation></semantics></math>,
we obtain</p>
<table id="S3.EGx14" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}})-\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}})-\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})]</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}\!+\!\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Merge}}\!-\!\mathbf{W}^{*})^{\top}\mathbf{H}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Merge}}-\mathbf{W}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.052em">+</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.052em">−</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}\!+\!\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Merge}}\!-\!\mathbf{W}^{*})^{\top}\mathbf{H}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Merge}}-\mathbf{W}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\quad+\tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{H}\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})+\tfrac{L_{H}}{6}\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\quad+\tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{H}\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})+\tfrac{L_{H}}{6}\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Due to <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}\leq\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}\leq\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}\leq\delta\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}\leq\delta\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and hence
<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}\leq\delta\,\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}\leq\delta\,\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Moreover, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}=\|\mathbb{E}\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}+\mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{\phi}))=\|\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Merge}}-\mathbf{W}^{*}\|_{2}^{2}+\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Cov</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}=\|\mathbb{E}\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}+\mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{\phi}))=\|\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Merge}}-\mathbf{W}^{*}\|_{2}^{2}+\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Finally, using <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}\preceq L\mathbf{I}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐇</mi><mo>⪯</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐈</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}\preceq L\mathbf{I}</annotation></semantics></math> yields the bound in terms of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})</annotation></semantics></math>.
The same argument applies to
<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math> individually.
The full derivation is provided in Appendix <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Results ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>.
 <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\square" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\square</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem6" title="Theorem 3.6. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.6</span></a> indicates that the excess loss upper bound is primarily controlled by the trace term.
For the merged model, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})</annotation></semantics></math> depends on the mixing weights <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}})</annotation></semantics></math>.
In the following, we minimize this trace term to obtain the optimal mixing weights in closed form.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.7</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Minimizing the trace term <math id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})</annotation></semantics></math> yields the optimal mixing weights, given by</span></p>
<table id="S3.EGx15" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E17"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{*}=\frac{b-c}{a+b-2c},\qquad\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}}^{*}=\frac{a-c}{a+b-2c}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{*}=\frac{b-c}{a+b-2c},\qquad\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}}^{*}=\frac{a-c}{a+b-2c},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),\,b=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}),\,c=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),\,b=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}),\,c=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}).</annotation></semantics></math>
At this optimum, the merged trace is smaller than those of the two individual models:</span></p>
<table id="S3.EGx16" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E18"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})\leq\min\{\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),\,\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})\}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})\leq\min\{\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),\,\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">At the optimal weights <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\lambda^{*}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\lambda^{*}_{\mathrm{Local}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\lambda^{*}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\lambda^{*}_{\mathrm{Local}})</annotation></semantics></math> in Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem7" title="Lemma 3.7. ‣ Proof sketch of Theorem . ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.7</span></a>, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})</annotation></semantics></math> attains its minimum.
Moreover, this minimum satisfies <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})\leq\min\{\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),\,\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})\leq\min\{\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),\,\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Therefore, by Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem6" title="Theorem 3.6. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.6</span></a> and Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem7" title="Lemma 3.7. ‣ Proof sketch of Theorem . ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.7</span></a>, the merged model admits an excess loss upper bound that is tighter than the bounds for FedIT or local fine-tuning alone.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Estimation of Fisher Information Matrix</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Section <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>, we established that <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}=\mathbf{F}_{\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}}^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐅</mi><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}=\mathbf{F}_{\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}}^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}=\mathbf{F}_{\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}}^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐅</mi><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}=\mathbf{F}_{\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}}^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., each posterior variance is given by the inverse Fisher information matrix.
To reduce the computation cost, we adopt a diagonal approximation
of the Fisher information matrix <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Matena and Raffel, 2022</a>)</cite>.
The diagonal Fisher matrix evaluated at the posterior mean <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is given by</p>
<table id="S3.EGx17" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E19"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\widehat{\mathbf{F}}_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}\!\!" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐅</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\widehat{\mathbf{F}}_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}\!\!</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E19.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\!\text{diag}\!\bigg(\!\frac{1}{N}\!\!\sum_{n=1}^{N}\!\mathbb{E}_{\bm{y}\sim p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}(\bm{y}\mid\bm{x}_{n})}\!\!\left[\!\big(\nabla_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}\!\log p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}(\bm{y}\!\!\mid\!\!\bm{x}_{n})\big)^{\odot 2}\right]\!\!\bigg)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo rspace="0.108em">=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.736em;" width="1.736em"><mtext>diag</mtext></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>𝒚</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝒚</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mpadded style="width:0.410em;" width="0.410em"><mi>𝒚</mi></mpadded><mpadded style="width:0em;" width="0em"><mo fence="true">∣</mo></mpadded><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mpadded style="width:0em;" width="0em"><mo>]</mo></mpadded></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\!\text{diag}\!\bigg(\!\frac{1}{N}\!\!\sum_{n=1}^{N}\!\mathbb{E}_{\bm{y}\sim p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}(\bm{y}\mid\bm{x}_{n})}\!\!\left[\!\big(\nabla_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}\!\log p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}(\bm{y}\!\!\mid\!\!\bm{x}_{n})\big)^{\odot 2}\right]\!\!\bigg),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is the mini-batch size to estimate the Fisher information and <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\cdot)^{\odot 2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\cdot)^{\odot 2}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the element-wise square operator.
Consequently, the posterior variance can be approximated as <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{i}\approx(\widehat{\mathbf{F}}_{\bm{\mu}_{i}})^{{-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐅</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{i}\approx(\widehat{\mathbf{F}}_{\bm{\mu}_{i}})^{{-1}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To approximate the cross-covariance between the two task vectors, we compute per-sample
gradients under <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math>, estimate their coordinate-wise variances and covariance,
and obtain a gradient correlation coefficient <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> for each parameter dimension.
We then construct a diagonal approximation</p>
<table id="S3.EGx18" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E20"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}})_{kk}\;\approx\;\rho_{k}\sqrt{(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}})_{kk}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})_{kk}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">≈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}})_{kk}\;\approx\;\rho_{k}\sqrt{(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}})_{kk}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})_{kk}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the parameter coordinate and <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is clipped to ensure <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\succeq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪰</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\succeq 0</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S3.SS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪯</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Further details on the estimation procedure and computation times are provided in the Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Implementation ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> and <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Computation Time ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5 </span>Communication Overhead Comparison</h3>

<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We denote <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> as the number of communication rounds.
FedIT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2024</a>)</cite> uploads both <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐀</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐁</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{B}</annotation></semantics></math> each round, yielding per-client overhead <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(r(m+n)T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(r(m+n)T)</annotation></semantics></math>.
FedSA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2025</a>)</cite> uploads only <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐀</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}</annotation></semantics></math>, yielding <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(rnT)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(rnT)</annotation></semantics></math>.
FFA-LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2024</a>)</cite> uploads only <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐁</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{B}</annotation></semantics></math>, yielding <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(rmT)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(rmT)</annotation></semantics></math>.
FedDPA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2024</a>)</cite> uploads one of two locally trained LoRA modules per round, yielding <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(r(m+n)T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(r(m+n)T)</annotation></semantics></math>.
FedALT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bian et al., 2026</a>)</cite> uploads the local LoRA module each round, yielding <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(r(m+n)T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(r(m+n)T)</annotation></semantics></math>.
For <span id="S3.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span>, clients upload both <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐀</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐁</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{B}</annotation></semantics></math> only during the FedIT phase, so the overhead is <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(r(m+n)T_{\text{FedIT}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>FedIT</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(r(m+n)T_{\text{FedIT}})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\text{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>FedIT</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\text{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes
the number of communication rounds required to train the FedIT model.
The communication overhead comparison is summarized in Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3.5 Communication Overhead Comparison ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.
<span id="S3.SS5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> achieves consistent performance gains even under a reduced communication budget.
A detailed performance-communication trade-off is reported in Section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Performance-Communication Trade-Off ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>

<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we evaluate and compare the performance of the proposed <span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> against baseline methods on vision and language benchmarks.
The baseline methods
include Local fine-tuning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, FedIT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, FFA-LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, FedSA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, FedDPA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, FedALT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bian et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, and Fisher Merging <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Matena and Raffel, 2022</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>

<td id="S4.tab1.1.1.2.12" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S4.tab1.1.1.2.12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">Avg.</span></td></tr>
