<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Vision Benchmark</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We adopt ViT-B/16 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dosovitskiy et al., 2021</a>)</cite> as the pre-trained model.
To simulate label heterogeneity, we partition CIFAR-100 across clients using a Dirichlet distribution with concentration parameter <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.
For each client, we construct both the training and test splits according to the same Dirichlet-based partition.
Unless otherwise specified, we consider <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> clients.
All federated baselines are trained for 600 communication rounds.
For both Fisher merging and the proposed <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span>, we first train the FedIT model and the local fine-tuning model for 400 and 300 rounds, respectively, and then merge the two models to obtain the final model.
As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, the proposed <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> achieves the best overall performance among all baseline methods, outperforming the strongest baseline, FedDPA, by an average accuracy margin of 3.41.
Moreover, <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> reduces the communication cost by 33.3% compared to FedDPA, FedALT, and FedIT.
See Section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Performance-Communication Trade-Off ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> and Figure <a href="#S4.F2.sf1" title="Figure 2(a) ‣ Figure 2 ‣ 4.2 Language Benchmark ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(a)</span></a> for a detailed performance-communication trade-off analysis.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Language Benchmark</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next evaluate <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> on LLM and NLP benchmark.
We adopt LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dubey et al., 2024</a>)</cite> as the pre-trained model and construct a task-heterogeneous setting by assigning each client a distinct task from the commonsense reasoning benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and report accuracy for all tasks.
Each client has 1,000 training examples and 500 test examples.
All federated baseline methods are trained for 600 communication rounds, while the local fine-tuning baseline is trained for 300 rounds to prevent overfitting.
Since Fisher merging requires estimating Fisher information for all model parameters, it is computationally prohibitive for LLMs with over 1B parameters.
In contrast, <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> computes Fisher information only for the LoRA module, substantially reducing the number of parameters involved and making the computation tractable.
For <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span>, we train FedIT for 50 rounds and local fine-tuning for 300 rounds, and then merge the resulting models to obtain the final personalized model for each client.
As reported in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> consistently outperforms all baselines across the evaluated NLP tasks.
In particular, <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> achieves the highest average accuracy, improving upon the strongest baseline by 1.85.
Moreover, <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> achieves these improvements with a very small communication overhead. See Section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Performance-Communication Trade-Off ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> and Figure <a href="#S4.F2.sf2" title="Figure 2(b) ‣ Figure 2 ‣ 4.2 Language Benchmark ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(b)</span></a> for a detailed performance-communication trade-off analysis.
The gains observed across both large vision (ViT) and language models (LLaMA) demonstrate that <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> generalizes well across model families, parameter scales, and task types.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F2" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">

</figure></div></div>

<span id="S4.F2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> (<math id="S4.F2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>) denotes our method where the FedIT model obtained at communication round <math id="S4.F2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> is used for merging.
<span id="S4.F2.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> achieves strong performance with substantially lower communication overhead than baselines.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Performance-Communication Trade-Off</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this subsection, we compare the communication overhead of all methods.
In ViT-B/16 model, the LoRA adaptation introduces 147,456 parameters to the <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐀</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> matrices and 147,456 parameters to the <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐁</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{B}</annotation></semantics></math> matrices, with each equivalent to 0.59 MB when stored in float32 precision.
In LLaMa-3.2-3B-Instruct model, the LoRA adaptation introduces 2,064,384 parameters to the <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐀</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> matrices and 1,146,880 parameters to the <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐁</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{B}</annotation></semantics></math> matrices, with equivalent to 8.26 MB and 4.59 MB when stored in float32 precision.
<span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> (<math id="S4.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>) denotes our method where the FedIT model obtained at communication round <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> is used for merging with the local model at round 300.
Fig. <a href="#S4.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 4.2 Language Benchmark ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows that <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> consistently achieves the best performance-communication trade-off.
In particular, <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> attains the highest accuracy while requiring substantially less communication than FedIT, FedALT, and FedDPA.
Moreover, compared to low-communication baselines, FedSA and FFA-LoRA, <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> delivers clear performance gains at comparable overhead, demonstrating robust communication efficiency across different backbones and benchmarks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Performance Gain of Model Merging</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this subsection, we show the performance gain by model merging over the FedIT and local models.
Specifically, we compare the merged model <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> with the FedIT model and the local model.
For the vision benchmark, <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> is obtained by merging the FedIT model trained for 400 rounds with the local model trained for 300 rounds.
Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.4 Performance Gain of Model Merging ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> shows that <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> achieves <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65.21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>65.21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65.21</annotation></semantics></math> accuracy, improving the local baseline by <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.32</annotation></semantics></math> and the FedIT baseline by <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.33" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7.33</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.33</annotation></semantics></math>.
For the commonsense reasoning benchmark, <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> is obtained by merging the FedIT model trained for 50 rounds with the local model trained for 300 rounds.
Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.4 Performance Gain of Model Merging ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows that <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> achieves <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="74.18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>74.18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">74.18</annotation></semantics></math> accuracy, improving the local baseline by <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.13</annotation></semantics></math> and the FedIT baseline by <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6.45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.45</annotation></semantics></math>.
These results indicate that model merging can effectively combine the global knowledge from FedIT model with the personalized knowledge from local fine-tuning model, leading to a substantial accuracy gain.</p>
</div>

<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Ablation Study</h3>

<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Effect of FedIT model round for merging:</span>
We examine the effect of the FedIT training round used for merging.
Specifically, we fix the local fine-tuning model at round 300 and merge it with FedIT checkpoints trained for different numbers of rounds.
As shown in Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.4 Performance Gain of Model Merging ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>a and Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.4 Performance Gain of Model Merging ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>b, <span id="S4.SS5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> improves steadily as the FedIT model is trained longer on both benchmarks, indicating that a better-optimized FedIT checkpoint provides stronger general knowledge that can be more effectively combined with the local model.
On personalized CIFAR-100 benchmark (Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.4 Performance Gain of Model Merging ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>a), increasing the FedIT training rounds yields a clear monotonic gain for the merged model (e.g., from 62.98 to 67.23).
On the commonsense reasoning benchmark (Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.4 Performance Gain of Model Merging ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>b), the merged model already achieves strong performance even when using an early FedIT checkpoint (e.g., round 50), despite the FedIT still improving substantially with more rounds.
This suggests that <span id="S4.SS5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> can effectively extract useful general knowledge from intermediate FedIT models and combine it with local model.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Effect of mixing weight strategy:</span>
We compare client performance using the mixing weights computed by our method with the best-performing weights selected by grid search over <math id="S4.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0,0.1,\ldots,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0,0.1,\ldots,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
As shown in Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.4 Performance Gain of Model Merging ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>c, the two bars are closely matched across clients, demonstrating that our computed weights achieve performance comparable to grid search while eliminating the expensive per-client hyperparameter sweep.
Moreover, Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.4 Performance Gain of Model Merging ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>c supports our theory and assumptions as the mixing weights computed by our method are close to the empirically optimal weights found via grid search.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Further experiments:</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Results with an increased number of clients and with a larger model are reported in Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Experiments with Increased Number of Clients ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a> and Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Experiments on FLAN benchmark ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>, respectively.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We proposed <span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span>, a principled personalization framework for federated fine-tuning that merges a federated model and a local model.
We approximate the federated and local task vectors as jointly Gaussian random variables and derive the upper bound on the expected excess task loss of the federated model, the local model, and their merged model, where the dominant term is a trace of the task vector variance.
By minimizing this bound, we obtain closed-form optimal mixing weights, guaranteeing that the merged model attains a tighter bound than both constituent models.
Experiment results show that <span id="S5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Potara</span> consistently improves client performance across both vision and language benchmarks, outperforming baselines while retaining communication efficiency.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper makes important contributions to federated personalization by developing a principled framework for personalized fine-tuning.
The focus of this work is on the technical advancement of large model fine-tuning.
While this research has potential societal impacts, it primarily addresses technical challenges and does not necessitate a specific discussion on societal consequences.</p>
</div>
</section>

<a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" title="Definition 2.1. ‣ 2.3 Linear Mode Connectivity ‣ 2 Preliminaries and Notation ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Definition 2.1</span></a>.
</span></li>
</ul>
</section>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Theoretical Results</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Derivation of Gaussian Distribution Approximation</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The gaussian distribution approximation has been used in prior works <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Matena and Raffel, 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tam et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, but the full derivation is omitted.
For completeness, we provide the full derivation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The training of the individual task vector for task <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> can be formulated as a maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problem <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Matena and Raffel, 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> as follows</p>
<table id="A1.EGx19" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E21"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E21.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\bm{\mu}_{i}\,=\,\arg\mathop{\max}_{\bm{\theta}_{i}}\,p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.448em" rspace="0.448em">=</mo><mi>arg</mi><munder><mo lspace="0.167em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">max</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></munder><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="false" rspace="0.337em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\bm{\mu}_{i}\,=\,\arg\mathop{\max}_{\bm{\theta}_{i}}\,p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the dataset associated with task <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>.
Here, task <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> may correspond either to the FedIT objective or to the local fine-tuning objective.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We perform a second-order Taylor expansion of the log-posterior around a point <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\bm{\theta}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\bm{\theta}}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A1.EGx20" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E22"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E22.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\approx\log p(\hat{\bm{\theta}}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})+(\bm{\theta}_{i}-\hat{\bm{\theta}})^{\top}\nabla_{\bm{\theta}_{i}}\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})|_{\bm{\theta}_{i}=\hat{\bm{\theta}}}-\frac{1}{2}(\bm{\theta}_{i}-\hat{\bm{\theta}})^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\bm{\theta}_{i}-\hat{\bm{\theta}})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\approx\log p(\hat{\bm{\theta}}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})+(\bm{\theta}_{i}-\hat{\bm{\theta}})^{\top}\nabla_{\bm{\theta}_{i}}\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})|_{\bm{\theta}_{i}=\hat{\bm{\theta}}}-\frac{1}{2}(\bm{\theta}_{i}-\hat{\bm{\theta}})^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\bm{\theta}_{i}-\hat{\bm{\theta}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(22)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{i}=-\nabla^{2}_{\bm{\theta}_{i}}\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})|_{\bm{\theta}_{i}=\hat{\bm{\theta}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><msub><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{i}=-\nabla^{2}_{\bm{\theta}_{i}}\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})|_{\bm{\theta}_{i}=\hat{\bm{\theta}}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We assume that the parameter <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> of
the trained neural network is a local maximum of the posterior distribution.
By setting <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\bm{\theta}}=\bm{\mu}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\bm{\theta}}=\bm{\mu}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\bm{\theta}_{i}}\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})|_{\bm{\theta}_{i}=\bm{\mu}_{i}}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\bm{\theta}_{i}}\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})|_{\bm{\theta}_{i}=\bm{\mu}_{i}}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Then, we obtain</p>
<table id="A1.EGx21" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E23"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})\approx\log p(\bm{\mu}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})-\frac{1}{2}(\bm{\theta}_{i}-\bm{\mu}_{i})^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\bm{\theta}_{i}-\bm{\mu}_{i})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})\approx\log p(\bm{\mu}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})-\frac{1}{2}(\bm{\theta}_{i}-\bm{\mu}_{i})^{\top}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\bm{\theta}_{i}-\bm{\mu}_{i}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(23)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p5.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}_{i}=-\nabla^{2}_{\bm{\theta}_{i}}\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})|_{\bm{\theta}_{i}=\bm{\mu}_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><msub><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}_{i}=-\nabla^{2}_{\bm{\theta}_{i}}\log p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})|_{\bm{\theta}_{i}=\bm{\mu}_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Applying the Laplace approximation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">MacKay, 1992</a>; <a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Daxberger et al., 2021</a>)</cite> around the local optimum <math id="A1.SS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, the posterior distribution <math id="A1.SS1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> admits the following Gaussian approximation:</p>
<table id="A1.EGx22" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E24"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})\approx\mathcal{N}(\bm{\theta}_{i};\bm{\mu}_{i},\mathbf{H}_{i}^{-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.170em">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle p(\bm{\theta}_{i}\,|\,\mathcal{D}_{i})\approx\mathcal{N}(\bm{\theta}_{i};\bm{\mu}_{i},\mathbf{H}_{i}^{-1})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(24)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p6.2" class="ltx_p">Equivalently, we write</p>
<table id="A1.EGx23" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E25"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\bm{\theta}_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(\bm{\mu}_{i},\bm{\Sigma}_{i})\quad\text{where}\,\bm{\Sigma}_{i}=\mathbf{H}_{i}^{-1}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mtext>where</mtext><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐇</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\bm{\theta}_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(\bm{\mu}_{i},\bm{\Sigma}_{i})\quad\text{where}\,\bm{\Sigma}_{i}=\mathbf{H}_{i}^{-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Given a trained neural network model <math id="A1.SS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}(\bm{y}\mid\bm{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝒚</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>𝒙</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}(\bm{y}\mid\bm{x})</annotation></semantics></math>, the Fisher information matrix <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Matena and Raffel, 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fisher, 1922</a>)</cite> is defined as</p>
<table id="A1.EGx24" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E26"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbf{F}_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}=\mathbb{E}_{\bm{x}}\Big[\mathbb{E}_{\bm{y}\sim p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}\!(\bm{y}\mid\bm{x})}\big[\nabla_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}\log p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}(\bm{y}\mid\bm{x})\nabla_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}\log p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}(\bm{y}\mid\bm{x})^{\top}\big]\Big]." display="inline" maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>𝒚</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝒚</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>𝒙</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝒚</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝒚</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>𝒙</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbf{F}_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}=\mathbb{E}_{\bm{x}}\Big[\mathbb{E}_{\bm{y}\sim p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}\!(\bm{y}\mid\bm{x})}\big[\nabla_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}\log p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}(\bm{y}\mid\bm{x})\nabla_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}\log p_{\bm{\mu}_{i}}(\bm{y}\mid\bm{x})^{\top}\big]\Big].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p7.2" class="ltx_p">It can be shown that the Fisher information matrix coincides with the Hessian at modes of the distribution <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pascanu and Bengio, 2013</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Proof of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem6" title="Theorem 3.6. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.6</span></a></h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recall that the joint distribution of <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}},\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}})</annotation></semantics></math> is given by</p>
<table id="A1.EGx25" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E27"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\\
\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}}\end{bmatrix}\sim\mathcal{N}\bigg(\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\\
\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}&amp;\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\\
\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}^{\top}&amp;\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}\end{bmatrix}\bigg)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">(</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msubsup><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\\
\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Local}}\end{bmatrix}\sim\mathcal{N}\bigg(\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\\
\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Local}}\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}&amp;\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\\
\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}^{\top}&amp;\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}\end{bmatrix}\bigg).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the cross-covariance between the two task vectors with
<math id="A1.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\succeq\mathbf{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪰</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\succeq\mathbf{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪯</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A1.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪯</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Then, the merged task vector follows the following Gaussian distribution:</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(28)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where</p>
<table id="A1.EGx27" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E29"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>

</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To analyze the effect of model merging, we expand the task loss <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}</annotation></semantics></math> around its optimum <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\phi}\;=\;\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}}-\mathbf{W}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\phi}\;=\;\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}}-\mathbf{W}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{H}\;=\;\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{H}\;=\;\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the pre-trained model that can be regarded as a constant vector.
By Assumption <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem4" title="Assumption 3.4. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a> and Lemma 2.2 in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Carmon et al., 2018</a>)</cite>, we have</p>
<table id="A1.EGx28" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E33"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}})\leq\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})+\frac{1}{2}\,\bm{\phi}^{\top}\mathbf{H}\,\bm{\phi}+\frac{L_{H}}{6}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>Pre</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐇</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{Pre}}+\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}})\leq\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{W}^{*})+\frac{1}{2}\,\bm{\phi}^{\top}\mathbf{H}\,\bm{\phi}+\frac{L_{H}}{6}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>

<p id="A1.SS2.p5.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Merge}}=\mathbb{E}[\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{Merge}}=\mathbb{E}[\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}}]</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A1.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}}=\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Cov</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜽</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}}=\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{\theta}_{\mathrm{Merge}})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">By Assumption <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Assumption 3.2. ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>, we have <math id="A1.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}\leq\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}\leq\delta</annotation></semantics></math>,
and therefore <math id="A1.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}\leq\delta\,\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}\leq\delta\,\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Taking expectation yields <math id="A1.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}\leq\delta\,\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{3}\leq\delta\,\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\phi}\|_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
By the second-moment decomposition, we have</p>
<table id="A1.EGx31" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E36"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

i\in\{\mathrm{FedIT},\mathrm{Local}\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(39)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Proof of Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem7" title="Lemma 3.7. ‣ Proof sketch of Theorem . ‣ 3.3 Determination of Mixing Weights ‣ 3 Our Method: Potara ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.7</span></a></h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let</p>
<table id="A1.EGx35" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E40"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E40.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle a=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),\quad b=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}),\quad c=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle a=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),\quad b=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}),\quad c=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(40)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Hence</p>
<table id="A1.EGx36" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E41"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E41.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E41.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{tr}(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{2}\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}}^{2}\cdot\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}+\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}^{\top}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{tr}(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{2}\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}}^{2}\cdot\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}+\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}^{\top}))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(41)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A1.E42"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E42.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{2}\cdot a+\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}}^{2}\cdot b+2\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}}\cdot c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{2}\cdot a+\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}}^{2}\cdot b+2\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\lambda_{\mathrm{Local}}\cdot c</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(42)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Using the Lemma <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem2" title="Lemma A.2. ‣ A.4 Proof of Lemmas ‣ Appendix A Theoretical Results ‣ Communication-Efficient Personalized Adaptation via Federated-Local Model Merging" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>,
we have</p>
<table id="A1.EGx37" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E43"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E43.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle|c|\;=\;|\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}})|\;\leq\;\sqrt{\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}})\,\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})}\;=\;\sqrt{ab}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>c</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>tr</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle|c|\;=\;|\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}})|\;\leq\;\sqrt{\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}})\,\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})}\;=\;\sqrt{ab}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(43)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We define a function <math id="A1.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to <math id="A1.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> as follows</p>
<table id="A1.EGx38" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E44"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E44.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle g(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}})=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})=a\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{2}+b(1-\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}})^{2}+2\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}(1-\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}})c," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle g(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}})=\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})=a\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{2}+b(1-\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}})^{2}+2\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}(1-\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}})c,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(44)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS3.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leq\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leq\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This quadratic form is convex in <math id="A1.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
because <math id="A1.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="g^{{}^{\prime\prime}}(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}})=2(a+b-2c)\geq 2(a+b-2\sqrt{ab})=2(\sqrt{a}-\sqrt{b})^{2}\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>′′</mo></msup></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mi>a</mi></msqrt><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mi>b</mi></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{{}^{\prime\prime}}(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}})=2(a+b-2c)\geq 2(a+b-2\sqrt{ab})=2(\sqrt{a}-\sqrt{b})^{2}\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Then, we obtain the optimal <math id="A1.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> and the optimum as</p>
<table id="A1.EGx39" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E45"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E45.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{*}=\frac{b-c}{a+b-2c}\in\,[0,1]," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo rspace="0.448em">∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{*}=\frac{b-c}{a+b-2c}\in\,[0,1],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(45)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<table id="A1.EGx40" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E46"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E46.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle g(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{*})=b-\frac{(b-c)^{2}}{a+b-2c}=a-\frac{(a-c)^{2}}{a+b-2c}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle g(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{*})=b-\frac{(b-c)^{2}}{a+b-2c}=a-\frac{(a-c)^{2}}{a+b-2c}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(46)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Due to <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪯</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo>⪯</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}}\preceq\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math>, it follows that <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}})\leq\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}})\leq\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}})\leq\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Cross</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Local</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Cross}})\leq\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Local}})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Combining both inequalities yields <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\leq\min(a,b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\leq\min(a,b)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Therefore, the optimum is smaller than <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{*})\leq\min\{a,b\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(\lambda_{\mathrm{FedIT}}^{*})\leq\min\{a,b\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p7.1" class="ltx_p">So far, we have shown that, at the optimal mixing weights <math id="A1.SS3.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda^{*}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>FedIT</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda^{*}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS3.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda^{*}_{\mathrm{Local}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>Local</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda^{*}_{\mathrm{Local}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS3.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>Merge</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{Merge}})</annotation></semantics></math> is smaller than <math id="A1.SS3.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\min\{\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝚺</mi><mi>FedIT</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\min\{\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}}),\mathrm{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{\mathrm{FedIT}})\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Therefore, the merged model admits an excess loss upper bound that is tighter than the bounds for FedIT or local
fine-tuning alone.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">

<div id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}=\mathbb{E}[\bm{\phi}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝛍</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}=\mathbb{E}[\bm{\phi}]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\Sigma}=\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{\phi})=\mathbb{E}\big[(\bm{\phi}-\bm{\mu})(\bm{\phi}-\bm{\mu})^{\top}\big]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝚺</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Cov</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ϕ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝛍</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ϕ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝛍</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\Sigma}=\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{\phi})=\mathbb{E}\big[(\bm{\phi}-\bm{\mu})(\bm{\phi}-\bm{\mu})^{\top}\big]</annotation></semantics></math>.
We have</span></p>

<math id="A1.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{AB})=\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{BA})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐀𝐁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐁𝐀</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{AB})=\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{BA})</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
